title: Erdős #1011 (OQ-01): Mantel's Theorem — the Triangle Case, Axiom-Free
description: Discharges the triangle base case of Erdős Problem #1011. The parent file axiomatizes the extremal edge counts forcing triangles; the smallest, f_2(n), is Mantel's theorem (1907) — the r=2 case of Turán's theorem: a triangle-free graph on n vertices has at most ⌊n²/4⌋ edges, sharply attained by the balanced complete bipartite graph. Using Mathlib 4.26.0's Turán machinery (SimpleGraph.CliqueFree.card_edgeFinset_le, card_edgeFinset_turanGraph), this entry proves the bound, its cleared-denominator form 4·#edges ≤ n², that the Turán graph turanGraph n 2 is triangle-free with the exact edge count (n²−(n%2)²)/4, and sharpness for even n. Self-contained (Mathlib-only), 0 axioms, 0 sorries; host-verified via lake env lean.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős Problem #1011 asks for $f_r(n)$, the least number of edges that forces a triangle in an $n$-vertex graph of chromatic number at least $r$. The asymptotics involve a factor $g(r) \sim r^2 \log r$ and the general problem is open. The small cases are classical: $f_2(n) = \lfloor n^2/4\rfloor + 1$ is **Mantel's theorem** (Willem Mantel, 1907), and $f_3(n) = \lfloor (n-1)^2/4\rfloor + 2$ is due to Erdős and Gallai. Mantel's theorem is the $r = 2$ special case of Turán's theorem (Pál Turán, 1941), the foundational result of extremal graph theory: among all $K_{r+1}$-free graphs on $n$ vertices, the balanced complete $r$-partite graph (the Turán graph) has the most edges.
overview.problemStatement: The parent formalization `Erdos1011Problem.lean` records the triangle base case as an axiom (`turan_theorem`). Can it instead be proved? Concretely: show that every triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices has at most $\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$ edges, that this bound is sharp, and that the extremal graph is the balanced complete bipartite graph — all without axioms, using Lean's Mathlib library.
overview.proofStrategy: Mathlib 4.26.0 now contains the full Turán development. A triangle is a 3-clique, so 'triangle-free' is `G.CliqueFree 3`, and the relevant Turán parameter is `r = 2`. Specializing `SimpleGraph.CliqueFree.card_edgeFinset_le` to `r = 2` gives `#edges ≤ (n² − (n%2)²)·1/4 + (n%2).choose 2`. The binomial correction `(n%2).choose 2` vanishes because `n % 2 ≤ 1 < 2` (`Nat.choose_eq_zero_of_lt`), and `(n² − (n%2)²)/4 ≤ n²/4` by monotonicity of `Nat` division over subtraction, yielding `#edges ≤ n²/4`. The cleared-denominator form follows from `Nat.mul_div_le`. Sharpness comes from `card_edgeFinset_turanGraph` (the exact count of `turanGraph n 2`) together with `turanGraph_cliqueFree`; for even `n` the modular term is zero and the count is exactly `n²/4`.
keyInsights: Identifying the parent's axiom with an existing Mathlib theorem is the whole game: 'triangle-free' = `CliqueFree 3`, 'no $K_{r+1}$' with $r = 2$. Once the dictionary is fixed, the Erdős #1011 triangle axiom is a specialization of `CliqueFree.card_edgeFinset_le`, not a new proof obligation.

Mathlib states the Turán bound with exact integer-arithmetic correction terms `(n² − (n%r)²)(r−1)/(2r) + (n%r).choose 2`. The work of specialization is arithmetic hygiene: at `r = 2` the binomial term is identically 0 (since `n % 2 < 2`) and the subtraction only decreases the bound, so the clean `⌊n²/4⌋` form drops out by `Nat`-division monotonicity.

Sharpness is not folklore here — it is exhibited by a concrete witness. `turanGraph n 2` is proved triangle-free and its edge count is computed exactly as `(n² − (n%2)²)/4`, which equals `n²/4` precisely when `n` is even. This turns 'the bound is best possible' into a checked existence statement.

Converting `turan_theorem` from axiom to theorem is genuine axiom elimination for the Erdős #1011 family: the triangle case is now machine-checked rather than assumed, reducing the trusted base of the development.

sections.title: Module Header and Lineage
sections.summary: Imports Mathlib; module docstring explaining that this discharges the triangle (r=2) base case of Erdős #1011, which the parent file axiomatizes. Opens SimpleGraph and sets up the variable context (finite vertex type, decidable adjacency).

sections.title: Mantel's Bound
sections.summary: `triangleFree_card_edgeFinset_le`: a triangle-free graph (CliqueFree 3) has ≤ n²/4 edges. Specializes `CliqueFree.card_edgeFinset_le` to r=2, kills the `(n%2).choose 2` term via `Nat.choose_eq_zero_of_lt`, and bounds by `n²/4` using division monotonicity.

sections.title: Cleared-Denominator Form
sections.summary: `four_mul_card_edgeFinset_le`: the integer-friendly restatement `4·#edges ≤ n²`, from the floor bound and `Nat.mul_div_le`.

sections.title: The Extremal Graph
sections.summary: `turanGraph_two_triangleFree`: the Turán graph turanGraph n 2 is triangle-free (from `turanGraph_cliqueFree`). `card_edgeFinset_turanGraph_two`: its exact edge count (n²−(n%2)²)/4, from `card_edgeFinset_turanGraph`.

sections.title: Sharpness for Even n
sections.summary: `mantel_sharp_even`: for even n, turanGraph n 2 is a triangle-free graph with exactly n²/4 edges, witnessing that Mantel's bound is best possible.

conclusion.summary: Proves Mantel's theorem — the triangle (r=2) base case of Erdős Problem #1011 — axiom-free from Mathlib's Turán machinery: triangle-free graphs have ≤ ⌊n²/4⌋ edges, with the balanced complete bipartite graph (turanGraph n 2) as a sharp witness for even n. This converts the parent file's `turan_theorem` axiom into a machine-checked theorem.
conclusion.implications: Mantel's theorem is the seed of extremal graph theory; the chromatic-threshold question of Erdős #1011 generalizes it to higher cliques and higher chromatic number. Having the triangle case verified gives a trustworthy anchor for the rest of the #1011 development and demonstrates that, as Mathlib's combinatorics library matures, axiomatized 'known results' can be progressively discharged.
openQuestions: Can the Erdős–Gallai f_3(n) = ⌊(n−1)²/4⌋ + 2 case (the parent's `erdos_gallai_theorem` axiom) similarly be derived from Mathlib, or does it require infrastructure (colour-critical edges) not yet present?

Mantel's bound is stated here as ⌊n²/4⌋; can the exact extremal characterization — that the *only* triangle-free graphs attaining it are complete balanced bipartite graphs — be formalized from Mathlib's `IsTuranMaximal` uniqueness results?
